pr_body:
This adds a function to escape ASS tags to remove code duplication between sub/osd_libass.c, console.lua, osc.lua, stats.lua and any user script that calls mp.create_osd_overlay().

 Always replacing \n with \\\\N in mangle_ass() even when it is not called by utils.escape_ass doesn't seem to cause any issue, but I made it conditional anyway to avoid changing how all OSD messages are treated unnecessarily.

Fixes #11209, fixes #11275.
pr_comments: Refactored to use a command that calls the existing `mangle_ass` C function instead of adding new scripting functions to reduce code duplication further.
Split into 2 commits. The 2nd one adds escaping to osc.lua.
Why a command over adding an API function to Lua/js?
avih requested converting the Lua and js functions to a command so there's a single ass escape implementation within mpv.
Well you could still call `osd_mangle_ass` from a Lua/js API implementation.

> avih requested converting the Lua and js functions to a command ...

I did not request this. I just said that your initial PR had 3 implementations, and reusing the existing one would be better. Regardless, I said then and I still think that we don't need this PR.

> Well you could still call `osd_mangle_ass` from a Lua/js API implementation.

I updated the PR as requested.
Updated to use autofree to prevent a memory leak if `pushlstring` OOMs (and we also noticed that `script_join_path` in `player/lua.c` should also use autofree to avoid this issue).

The C implementation does more than the original lua code which now uses the C API. At the very least it doesn't escape everything unconditionally - it allows unescaped parts between special bytes sequences, and it does some replacements for mpv internal font with other bytes sequences. I don't know whether or not it's desirable, but you should know if you change the behavior - and explain it at the commit message.

All clients can create ass overlays, but only lua/js clients are allowed access to the ass escape utility? Why? The trend and goal is to allow all clients access to the same scope of mpv utilities and values, unless it's strictly limited to things which run as internal mpv code. This has an additional value of using less internal lua/js specific code, and insted using global things in mpv. Just like `mp.get_mouse_pos()` was converted to a (new) property `mouse-pos` so that other clients can access it, and `utils.get_user_path()` was converted to the (new) command `expand-path`, and others. It's entirely reasonable that other clients would like to escape ass strings.

The new JS code has double free (one explicit, one by autofree).

The new JS docs is missing the argument.

At both the lua/js code, `bstr dst = (struct bstr){talloc_strdup(tmp, ""), 0};` doesn't need `(struct bstr)`, and arguably would be cleaner (and independent of the members order) as `{ .start = talloc... }`, though this could be considered personal taste (do check other places which initialize a `bstr` var with a literal value).

In `console.lua` it would be cleaner/simpler/smaller patch (and faster at runtime due to less names lookup) to replace the original function with `local ass_escape = utils.ass_escape` (with or without `local` - originally it was without, but should have been with) instead of replacing every instance of `ass_escape` with `utils.ass_escape`.

At the new `stats.lua` it can now error at `no_ASS(t)` if `t` is neither string nor number, while previously it explicitly first converted `t` to a string. Not sure if was used with non-number/string `t` (e.g. if some value hppens to be `nil`), but regardless, this change is not explained.

I think the second commit for `osc.lua` is questionable, and I think there could be reason to make the replacements which you removed (literal `\n`, dollar, whatever). I think you need to understand exactly which cases were addressed by the things which you removed, and ensure they still work correctly with the new code. I don't know what these use cases are, but you should know if you intend to change the behavior, and explain it at the commit message.

And regardless of the above, I still think we don't need this PR.

I restored the command implementation for now as that makes more sense to me too since C and JSON IPC clients can use it.

For osc.lua I believe the author (07ee7fb2c3) just didn't know how to escape backslashes by appending word joiners to them, and that's why he converted "\\\\n" to space instead of escaping it, and removed only trailing backslashes so anything that osc.lua adds after it isn't interpreted as a ASS tag. If you know how to escape backslash there is no reason not to do it properly. @wiiaboo can confirm this if you want confirmation from the author.

> And regardless of the above, I still think we don't need this PR.

@avih: Could you explain why? I think it is valid to fix #11209 and #11275, no?
I think this is perfectly fine approach to de-duplicate and unify escape code. If you think there are better ways to handle it implemented, feel free to send PR.

issue_context.title: On Windows OSC inserts line breaks or skips characters when \n is present in the file path
issue_context.body:
- mpv **0.35.1**
- Windows 10
- Source of the mpv binary: https://sourceforge.net/projects/mpv-player-windows/files/release/mpv-0.35.1-x86_64-v3.7z

### Reproduction steps

Play a file that contains `\n` or `\N` in the file path.

Examples:
file path: `L:\Videos\Music\nyan Cat - Copy.flv`
Shown in the OSC as:
![nyanCat](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25933468/216981152-ebc9a47d-c514-47ed-80d9-1db30181587f.png)

file path: `L:\Videos\Music\Nyan Cat.flv`
Shown in the OSC as:
![NyanCat2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25933468/216981141-8a5631fb-e612-4cae-871b-0ddc69c91e2d.png)

### Expected behavior

file name in the OSC interface should show the path as it is, without line breaks or skipping characters, such as:
file path: `L:\Videos\Music\Cat - Copy.flv`
Shown in the OSC as:
![cat](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25933468/216981061-b5091a12-77f0-4ad7-98d1-e81cf992bb6b.png)
